name: Shekel
overview: The shekel, defined in Scripture as a weight equal to twenty gerahs, served as a standard measure for weighing precious metals like gold and silver, as well as spices such as myrrh and cinnamon. It was used not only to weigh valuable items, exemplified by the golden earring of half a shekel weight in Genesis 24:22, but also functioned in the payment of offerings, fines, and fees, as highlighted in Exodus 30:13 and Numbers 3:47. The shekel had different standards, including the sanctuary shekel and the king's weight, ensuring accuracy and sanctity in transactions related to worship and civil duties.
